report.summary: The shop path and the platform are healthy at the sampled instants, but the orders-fulfillment Kafka pipeline is stalled: the orders-validator consumer stopped consuming permanently at offset 20 of topic orders-fulfillment after failing to parse one record ("Expecting value: line 1 column 35 (char 34)"), and its lag grew from 43 to 63 messages within ~40 s while the order-stream producer kept publishing every 2 s. The consumer code mounted from ConfigMap orders-pipeline-scripts reacts to a validation failure by pausing the partition in an endless sleep loop (with enable.auto.commit=false and max.poll.interval.ms=86400000), so the group never advances or rejoins. Trigger appears to be a malformed record at orders-fulfillment offset 20 (data-level; the producing object is not visible). Flagd fault-injection flags are all 'off', all 25 deployments are 1/1 ready with 0 pod restarts, and the only other errors seen (frontend 500s / locust 100% failure on POST /api/checkout at ~23:57:17) are startup transients while checkout was still starting (ECONNREFUSED on the checkout ClusterIP); they had stopped at the sampled times. The conclusion is partial because the whole stack, Prometheus series and Jaeger were (re)created at 23:56:42-23:57:46 and telemetry is only visible from ~23:57-23:58, so the onset of the poison record and any earlier incident cannot be observed, and Kafka tools never expose message content or the producer of offsets 0-19.

claims.text: Pod orders-validator-6d49bfb98d-hhd6z logged 'processed order_id=ORD-100019 committed_offset=20' and then 2026-11-23T23:57:48.330Z 'ERROR record validation failed at offset=20: Expecting value: line 1 column 35 (char 34)' followed by 'ERROR partition processing paused at offset=20'.

Consumer group orders-validator was at committed_offset 20 with end_offset 63 (lag 43) on orders-fulfillment partition 0 at 23:59:05, and its total lag on that topic was 63 at 23:59:46, i.e. the committed offset stayed at 20 while the log end kept growing.

The Kafka cluster itself is healthy at query time: 1 broker, 4 topics, 53 partitions, 0 under-replicated partitions, 0 offline partitions and no offline brokers.
The other order-pipeline consumers were current: group accounting committed_offset 19 vs end_offset 20 on topic orders (lag 1) and group fraud-detection committed_offset 21 vs end_offset 21 (lag 0).

All fault-injection flags in ConfigMap flagd-config are inactive: every entry (paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, cartFailure, adFailure, productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure, kafkaQueueProblems, imageSlowLoad, emailMemoryLeak, failedReadinessProbe, llmRateLimitError, llmInaccurateResponse, adHighCpu, adManualGc, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage) has defaultVariant 'off', and the flagd pod's init-config dump of the mounted demo.flagd.json shows the same 'defaultVariant: off' values.

Kubernetes workloads of the shop are healthy at query time: all 25 deployments in astronomy-shop report readyReplicas 1 / availableReplicas 1 with Available=True, and all 29 pods are Running and Ready with restartCount 0 (no OOMKilled, Evicted or BackOff state observed).

The only error spans recorded by the span metrics were 4 on frontend at 23:57:17 - POST /api/checkout (2), executing api route (pages) /api/checkout (1) and oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder (1) with http.status_code 500 / rpc.grpc.status_code 14 and detail '14 UNAVAILABLE: No connection established. Last error: connect ECONNREFUSED 10.96.157.159:8080 (2026-11-23T23:57:04.963Z)', i.e. the checkout ClusterIP while checkout was still starting.

Checkout itself worked in the same period: a sampled trace at 23:57:26 shows frontend POST /api/checkout returning http.status_code 200, oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder with rpc.grpc.status_code 0, PaymentService/Charge 0, CartService/EmptyCart 0 and email POST /send_order_confirmation 200, and the locust exporter's fail ratio for the load generator was 0 at 23:58:02.

No failure marks exist on the shop pods: the Unhealthy events in the window are startup-probe misses only (grafana readiness 23:56:49-23:56:50, opensearch-0 startup probe 23:56:53-23:57:03, otel-collector-agent readiness 23:56:47-23:57:18) plus Killing events for old otel-collector-agent DaemonSet pods (g5tdz, ksrjs, p4f5n), and no Evicted or OOMKilled reason was returned.

The environment is freshly (re)created: every shop pod's creationTimestamp lies between 2026-11-23T23:56:42Z and 2026-11-23T23:57:46Z, and the events list contains 25 Deployment ScalingReplicaSet, 25 ReplicaSet SuccessfulCreate and 43 Pod Started events for astronomy-shop in the last hour.

The trigger of the stall is a malformed record already present in orders-fulfillment at offset 20 (pre-seeded, not produced by order-stream): the records consumed at offsets 0-19 carried ids ORD-100000..ORD-100019, while the producer script and the order-stream log lines only ever emit 'ORD-' plus 12 hex characters, and no producer log line corresponds to offsets 0-19; the producing object for the bad record is therefore not identified.

Rejected: a flagd feature-flag fault injection caused the incident - all flags in flagd-config and in the flagd init-config dump are 'off' and the product-reviews service logged 'llmRateLimitError feature flag: False'.

Rejected: a crash/restart or resource failure of the shop workloads is the current incident - all deployments are 1/1 available, all pods have restartCount 0, and no OOMKilled, Evicted or Failed-phase evidence was returned.

Rejected: the pending alert 'HighRequestErrorRate POST /api/checkout (1.00)' reflected a lasting checkout failure - the underlying errors were startup ECONNREFUSED to checkout at 23:57:04-23:57:17, checkout traces return 200/grpc 0 afterwards and the locust fail ratio was 0 at 23:58:02.

Fix the consuming behaviour and the data: skip or dead-letter the unparseable orders-fulfillment record at offset 20 (or reset the group past it) instead of pausing the partition forever, remove the endless pause loop and the 24h max.poll.interval.ms from ConfigMap orders-pipeline-scripts/consumer.py, and alert on orders-validator consumer lag and on orders-processed staleness so a single bad record cannot silently stop the pipeline.

Kafka tools never return message content: the exact bytes of orders-fulfillment offset 20 and offsets 0-19 are unknown, and the producing object of offsets 0-19 is not identifiable from any log or object returned.
No offsets were read for topic orders-processed, so whether downstream output has stopped growing (versus only the orders-validator offset being frozen) is unverified.

The consumer script's behaviour was verified only from the mounted ConfigMap text (read of its logs was cut by the 60-line limit, incomplete view 7d3aab61-ec8d-43c1-8dcf-7a78709d9c0b-t1:5cc10438-e250-40c1-a998-71f71fc4caa0); Kubernetes change history for that ConfigMap is not available in this Run (change_history not integrated).

next_steps: Read the payload at orders-fulfillment offset 20 (for example kafka-console-consumer --offset 20 --max-messages 1) to characterise the malformed record and identify its origin, then decide whether to repair, drop, or dead-letter it.
After the fix, restart or manually advance consumer group orders-validator past offset 20 and confirm lag returns to 0 and orders-processed resumes.
Add lag-based alerting for orders-validator so a paused partition is detected automatically rather than inferred from logs.

content.consumer.py:
import json
import logging
import os
import signal
import time

from confluent_kafka import Consumer, Producer

logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(asctime)s %(levelname)s %(message)s")
log = logging.getLogger("orders-validator")

BOOTSTRAP = os.environ.get("KAFKA_BOOTSTRAP", "kafka:9092")
TOPIC = os.environ.get("ORDERS_TOPIC", "orders-fulfillment")
OUTPUT_TOPIC = os.environ.get("OUTPUT_TOPIC", "orders-processed")
GROUP = os.environ.get("CONSUMER_GROUP", "orders-validator")

_shutdown = False


def _request_shutdown(signum, frame):
    global _shutdown
    _shutdown = True


def process(value):
    obj = json.loads(value.decode("utf-8"))
    if "order_id" not in obj:
        raise ValueError("record has no 'order_id' field")
    return obj


def main():
    consumer = Consumer(
        {
            "bootstrap.servers": BOOTSTRAP,
            "group.id": GROUP,
            "enable.auto.commit": False,
            "auto.offset.reset": "earliest",
            "max.poll.interval.ms": 86400000,
        }
    )
    out = Producer({"bootstrap.servers": BOOTSTRAP, "enable.idempotence": True})
    consumer.subscribe([TOPIC])
    signal.signal(signal.SIGTERM, _request_shutdown)
    signal.signal(signal.SIGINT, _request_shutdown)
    log.info("orders-validator started bootstrap=%s topic=%s group=%s", BOOTSTRAP, TOPIC, GROUP)

    first = True
    while not _shutdown:
        msg = consumer.poll(1.0)
        if msg is None:
            continue
        if msg.error():
            log.warning("consumer error: %s", msg.error())
            continue

        if first:
            log.info("resuming partition at offset=%d", msg.offset())
            first = False

        try:
            order = process(msg.value())
        except Exception as exc:
            log.error("record validation failed at offset=%d: %s", msg.offset(), exc)
            log.error("partition processing paused at offset=%d", msg.offset())
            blocked = 0
            while not _shutdown:
                time.sleep(1)
                blocked += 1
                if blocked % 15 == 0:
                    log.error("partition remains paused at offset=%d", msg.offset())
            break

        result = json.dumps(
            {"source_offset": msg.offset(), "order_id": order["order_id"]},
            separators=(",", ":"),
        )
        out.produce(OUTPUT_TOPIC, value=result.encode("utf-8"))
        out.flush(10)
        consumer.commit(message=msg, asynchronous=False)
        log.info("processed order_id=%s committed_offset=%d", order["order_id"], msg.offset() + 1)

    out.flush(10)
    consumer.close()
    log.info("orders-validator stopped")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
content.producer.py:
import json
import logging
import os
import time
import uuid

from confluent_kafka import Producer

logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(asctime)s %(levelname)s %(message)s")
log = logging.getLogger("order-stream")

BOOTSTRAP = os.environ.get("KAFKA_BOOTSTRAP", "kafka:9092")
TOPIC = os.environ.get("ORDERS_TOPIC", "orders-fulfillment")
INTERVAL = float(os.environ.get("PRODUCE_INTERVAL_SEC", "2.0"))


def main():
    producer = Producer({"bootstrap.servers": BOOTSTRAP, "enable.idempotence": True})
    while True:
        order_id = "ORD-" + uuid.uuid4().hex[:12].upper()
        record = json.dumps({"order_id": order_id, "amount": 1 + int(uuid.uuid4().hex[:2], 16) % 7})
        producer.produce(TOPIC, value=record.encode("utf-8"))
        producer.poll(0)
        producer.flush(10)
        log.info("published order_id=%s", order_id)
        time.sleep(INTERVAL)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind. When the API server returns zero objects of a kind other than events (every page read), the result is ok with total_items_processed 0: it proves only that there were no objects matching this kind, namespace and selectors at query time, not that none existed during the incident. Zero events, or a list your filter reduced to nothing, stays no_data. metadata.managedFieldsSummary gives each manager's last write time only: it is not a full change history (earlier writes by the same manager are gone) and it does not say which fields that write changed.
